headline: High: shared MCP and overlapping network/tool surfaces create default prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks; MinerU’s offline isolation reduces but does not eliminate pairwise exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP surfaces and LightAgent can ingest browser/tool outputs while MinerU accepts document inputs via MCP/API. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if MinerU outputs are fed into LightAgent or vice versa. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are copied into LightAgent prompts or MCP messages
IF either agent treats file or tool output content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of peer outputs
Add a provenance tag to every inter-agent message
Route peer outputs through a human review step
Restrict MCP endpoints to read-only where possible
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches conversations, memory, tool results, and secrets, and has broad network egress; MinerU processes local documents and exposes API/MCP surfaces. If the pair shares a workspace or message channel, sensitive content can flow from LightAgent into MinerU outputs or from MinerU inputs into LightAgent’s egress path. The offline claim on MinerU lowers but does not remove risk.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, clipboard, or message queue
IF LightAgent forwards peer content through its network egress
IF MinerU is given documents containing secrets or personal data
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Block secret-bearing documents from the shared channel
Turn off LightAgent egress for peer-derived content
Use redaction before passing documents to MinerU
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on inter-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports subprocesses, browsers, broad egress, and multiple instances; MinerU supports concurrent inference and MCP/API access. Even though MinerU cannot write files or modify git state, both can act concurrently on shared mutable resources through MCP or networked workflows, so race/conflict risk exists in default multi-instance deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same MCP server or shared mutable backend
IF the orchestrator allows concurrent writes through networked tools
IF shared documents are edited while MinerU is extracting them
mitigations: Serialize access to shared backends
Assign disjoint resource scopes per agent
Disable concurrent writes during extraction runs
Use per-agent API credentials
requires-engineering: add locking around shared MCP resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can generate tool outputs and workflow state that MinerU may consume as document text or structured input. MinerU’s document-processing role suggests it may render or extract from that content without verifying upstream provenance. That makes a default pipeline vulnerable to propagating one agent’s mistakes into the other’s outputs, though not clearly to irreversible action-taking.
conditions: IF MinerU ingests LightAgent-generated text as authoritative source material
IF downstream automation trusts MinerU extraction without validation
IF LightAgent’s tool results are reused as facts in reports
mitigations: Require source citation checks before reuse
Compare extracted facts against original documents
Insert a verification step between agents
Mark peer-generated content as untrusted
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles secrets and broad network egress, while MinerU is documented as private/fully offline and touches local documents. This is a compliance mismatch only if regulated or sensitive data is routed from LightAgent into MinerU or vice versa; the profiles do not show a residency or certification conflict by default, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF regulated data is transferred from LightAgent to MinerU without a DPA or retention review
IF logs from either agent retain sensitive documents beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings for both agents
Disable verbose logging on sensitive runs
Review residency for any external API calls
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
